Playbook.name: Brute Force - O365 Failed Logins - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One source IP produced many O365 UserLoginFailed events (>=10 in the window) - password guessing/spray against cloud identities. This is the patched, lag-aware version. Triage: brute force from a real attacker source, or the egress NAT / a broken client?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A successful cloud-credential guess yields access to mail, files and potentially federated on-prem resources.

Assets.AssetType: Exchange Online, SharePoint/OneDrive, Teams, Entra directory

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: O365 unified audit via Elastic Agent (verified live). Fields: event.action, user.name, source.ip, o365.audit.Operation, o365.audit.ResultStatus, o365.audit.ObjectId, o365.audit.ModifiedProperties, o365.audit.Parameters, o365.audit.UserId. INGEST LAG 20-60 min - all queries use a 4h window and timestamp_override event.ingested at rule level.
JCB egress NAT is 94.249.88.0/24 - internal users appear from it.

Input.name: $source_ip
Input.description: Source IP of the failed logins.

Input.name: $username
Input.description: An affected account if the alert scopes one.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the failed-login burst is a real credential attack and whether any login then succeeded.

Step.name: Failed-login profile for this source
Step.Purpose: Breadth of accounts and error types distinguish spray (many users) from a single-account brute or a broken client.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE event.dataset == "o365.audit" AND event.action == "UserLoginFailed" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS fails = COUNT(*), users = COUNT_DISTINCT(user.name), errors = VALUES(o365.audit.LogonError), user_list = VALUES(user.name) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Many users + few fails each = spray; one user + many fails = brute; one user + one error repeated = a broken client/expired credential. Error InvalidUserNameOrPassword = guessing; DeviceAuthenticationFailed = client/service noise (excluded at rule level).

Step.name: Did any login SUCCEED from this source
Step.Purpose: A UserLoggedIn from the brute-forcing source after failures is the difference between attempt and compromise.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE event.dataset == "o365.audit" AND event.action == "UserLoggedIn" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS logins = COUNT(*), users = VALUES(user.name), first_success = MIN(@timestamp) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A success from the same source for a targeted account is strong compromise evidence - escalate and reset. No success = attempt only.

Node.Condition: A success (UserLoggedIn) from the brute-forcing source for a targeted account.
Node.Result: True Positive (Cloud Account Compromised - IR, reset + revoke tokens)

Node.Condition: Many accounts with InvalidUserNameOrPassword from an external (non-94.249.88.x) source, no success.
Source is the egress NAT 94.249.88.0/24 aggregating internal users, or one account with DeviceAuthenticationFailed (broken client).
External source, failures, but breadth/ownership unclear.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-O365BF-FAILS, INV-02-O365BF-SUCCESS to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Internal users behind the egress NAT, or a single broken client/service.

TruePositive.Definition: A real credential-guessing attack against cloud identities.

SOCAction.Item: Reset compromised accounts + revoke tokens; block the source; enforce CA/MFA.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A broken client/service repeatedly failing O365 auth.

Indicators.Item: One service account, one repeated error.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the stored credential/client config; track under credential-hygiene.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the change/actor in the audit log.
If unexpected/unauthorised, disable the actor session and reverse the change.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reverse the change; revoke sessions/tokens for the actor and affected principals.
Review the actor's other recent audit activity.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce MFA/conditional access; tighten admin consent and privileged-role governance (PIM); alert on these operations.

QualityChecks.Check: Account for O365 ingest lag (20-60 min) - short windows miss events; this rule uses event.ingested override.
Exclude the egress NAT 94.249.88.0/24 where source is used; tune known admin/automation via exceptions.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Compromised accounts reset + tokens revoked; source blocked.
